title: Jellyfin hangs after a bit of playback, especially on LXC
body: After some minutes of playback, usually 20–30, playback freezes and the Jellyfin server becomes unresponsive. The web client stops loading and connections time out. It happens with direct connections and through Traefik, from the same subnet or remotely, and across web, Findroid, and Swiftfin clients. I can reproduce it by selecting any media file, starting direct playback, and waiting. I am running unstable build 2024040805 on Debian 12 in a Proxmox LXC with 9 GB RAM, VirtIO networking, NFSv4 media storage, QSV on an Intel UHD 750, and FFmpeg 6.0.1-Jellyfin. The logs mention a WebSocket closing without completing its handshake and CustomAuthentication not being authenticated; clients report request timeouts and sometimes fragLoadTimeOut.

symptoms_visible: After roughly 20–30 minutes of playback, the video freezes, the web client no longer loads, and new connections to Jellyfin time out.
The same behavior occurs across web, Findroid, and Swiftfin clients and with either direct or reverse-proxy connections.
The logs mention an incomplete WebSocket close, while clients report request timeouts or fragLoadTimeOut.
N0.label: N0 playback-triggered server hang reported

symptoms_visible: The server froze after six minutes of playback even though about 8 GB of RAM and at least 3 GB of local storage were free.
SSH to the LXC remains responsive while Jellyfin connections time out.
The server can remain idle for days without becoming unavailable.
N1.label: N1 resource exhaustion and idle timeout ruled out

symptoms_visible: A fresh Ubuntu 22.04 LXC running the latest unstable build also became unresponsive after 14 minutes of playback.
N2.label: N2 fresh LXC reproduction

symptoms_visible: Playback still makes Jellyfin unresponsive in the LXC while the container itself remains reachable over SSH.
Rolling the same LXC back to the stable Jellyfin version avoids the hang without changing the container configuration.
N2_x.label: N2_x external LXC IO dismissal aftermath

symptoms_visible: The same unstable build played for two and a half hours in a full Debian VM without hanging, including a ten-minute test with four streams.
On affected LXC installations, 10.8.13 plays normally but the unresponsive playback behavior returns after upgrading the same installation to 10.9.
N3.label: N3 build and virtualization interaction isolated

symptoms_visible: When the lockup begins, Jellyfin's thread count rises continuously from its normal level of roughly 20–30 threads, adding about three threads every few seconds until the service is restarted.
Affected LXC users see lost WebSockets, playback-progress errors, and an unresponsive Jellyfin service even during direct play.
N4.label: N4 runaway thread signature observed

symptoms_visible: After updating to the build containing the maintainer's fix, an affected LXC installation can run a stream for most of the day without a freeze or an unresponsive server.
N_terminal.label: terminal fixed build verified by affected user

question_patterns: Can you monitor available RAM and disk space when the server hangs?
Does the LXC run out of memory or local storage during playback?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested again and had about 8 GB of RAM available and at least 3 GB of local storage free when it froze after six minutes. Transcoding is on tmpfs, but this was direct play.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: At the moment of the freeze, the container is out of RAM and its local filesystem is completely full.
There are about 7 GB of RAM and 4 GB of storage free instead, with the same freeze.

question_patterns: If you leave Jellyfin idle for the same amount of time, does its port become unavailable?
Can the server hang without any media playing?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. It can remain idle for days with no playback and is still fine whenever I connect.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Yes, it becomes unavailable after roughly the same interval even when nobody plays anything.

edges.comment: Reporter c2-c6: after being asked about RAM and disk, reporter measured resource headroom and volunteered that SSH to the LXC remained responsive. The reporter separately answered the idle-server probe and volunteered that the unchanged setup worked on 10.8.13.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce this in a fresh LXC installation?
Could you test a clean container with the current unstable build and report how long playback lasts?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I recreated it on a fresh Ubuntu 22.04 LXC running the latest unstable version. Playback hung after 14 minutes.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: A fresh LXC plays for several hours without any timeout, and the issue only occurs in my original configured container.

edges.comment: Reporter c10: reporter reproduced the original playback-triggered outage on a fresh Ubuntu LXC, reducing the likelihood that the original container's accumulated configuration caused it.

solution.intent: Dismiss the report as an LXC or storage IO hang outside Jellyfin's control, without treating the Jellyfin version-dependent behavior as a server regression.
solution.concrete_example: The hang appears limited to LXC and resembles blocked IO, so there may be nothing Jellyfin can change; investigate the host, mounts, and container instead.

edges.comment: Maintainer c14 proposed that the LXC reports looked like an uncontrollable IO hang. reporter c26-c32 and another affected LXC operator c44 later falsified that brush-off: the problematic build behaved differently by virtualization type, and the same LXC worked on 10.8.13 but failed after upgrading to 10.9.

question_patterns: Can you test a known problematic build in a full virtual machine rather than an LXC?
Does the same build hang under playback in a conventional VM?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested the same 2024040106 build in a full Debian 12 VM with the iGPU passed through. It was still fine after two and a half hours, and I also ran four streams for ten minutes without a hang.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The full VM hangs after the same six-to-fourteen-minute interval as the LXC.
The VM remains healthy for two hours rather than two and a half hours.

edges.comment: Reporter c21, c26-c32: reporter tested a known bad build in a full Debian VM and could not reproduce the hang. The target also folds c32 and affected LXC user c44, who compared old and new Jellyfin versions in otherwise unchanged LXC installations.

question_patterns: Before concluding this is only a host IO problem, can you run the same build in a full VM?
Can you compare the problematic build under LXC with the same build under a conventional VM?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran 2024040106 in a full Debian 12 VM with iGPU passthrough. It played for two and a half hours without hanging, and four simultaneous streams also stayed responsive during a ten-minute test.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same build hangs identically in both the full VM and the LXC.

edges.comment: Recovery from the c14 brush-off using reporter's c26-c32 comparison. The same-LXC version comparison is retained from the aftermath evidence and reinforced by a second affected LXC operator in c44.

question_patterns: Can you monitor the Jellyfin process when the lockup starts, especially its thread count?
What changes in btop or another process monitor at the moment Jellyfin becomes unresponsive?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Normally Jellyfin stays around 20–30 threads. As soon as the lockup starts, the count keeps rising by about three threads every couple of seconds and continues until I restart the process.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The thread count remains steady at about 25 throughout the outage, while the host reports the NFS mount blocked in uninterruptible IO.
The normal count is closer to 35, but it still rises continuously when Jellyfin stops responding.

edges.comment: Affected users participant10 and soakes c48-c49 first correlated the lockup with continuously spawning threads; idanbnn c50 reproduced the same signature with two streams. These affected LXC users are folded into the simulated user side. The unrelated Unraid database/WAL sub-problem discussed in c35-c39 is deliberately excluded.

solution.intent: Treat the playback outage as the confirmed Jellyfin server regression fixed by the maintainers, update to a build containing that fix, and have an affected user verify sustained playback before declaring resolution.
solution.concrete_example: Install Jellyfin 10.9.2 or another build containing the maintainer's fix, then repeat the affected playback workload while watching server responsiveness and thread count. An affected LXC user reported that a stream ran for most of the day without a freeze after this update.
solution.inference_hint: The thread only states that maintainers found and merged a fix; it does not describe the code-level mechanism. A correct answer should diagnose a Jellyfin server regression using the version, VM/LXC, and runaway-thread evidence without inventing undocumented fix internals.

edges.comment: Maintainers c52-c54 announced that the issue had been found and fixed. Affected LXC user danvirsen c56 then reported no freezes after updating, despite having reproduced them very frequently with one stream previously. The reporter did not personally provide this post-fix confirmation, so the terminal result is the folded affected user's own system evidence. The separate high-concurrency/same-file behavior in c55-c58 was directed to a new report and is not chained into this resolution.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted diagnosis at the level established by the thread: this was a Jellyfin server regression affecting playback on 10.9-era builds, with an observed runaway-thread signature; the thread does not disclose the code-level mechanism of the linked fix.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: ample RAM and disk remained, the LXC and SSH stayed responsive, idle operation was stable, a fresh LXC reproduced it, the same problematic build remained healthy in a full VM, and threads rose continuously when the lockup began.
Must not dismiss the issue solely as external LXC, NFS, or host IO behavior, and must not blame ordinary RAM or disk exhaustion; those directions are contradicted by the in-case comparisons.
Must recommend updating to a build containing the maintainer's fix rather than treating rollback or repeated service restarts as the permanent resolution.
Must ask an affected user to verify sustained playback and server responsiveness on a build containing the fix before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically proficient self-hoster who manages Proxmox LXC and full VMs, GPU passthrough, NFS storage, reverse proxies, and unstable Jellyfin builds; willing to create clean test environments and inspect process behavior.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and evidence-driven, with concise test reports and careful caveats when uncertain; willing to challenge a diagnosis when version-controlled comparisons contradict it.
